evidence.curator_note: RIBO panel (MH+ from permethylated ribofuranose; 76%). Book draws 1 arc; move <2> (C1-O7 heterolysis, both electrons routed onto the departing methanol oxygen) is the single arc drawn at the anomeric carbon; move <1> (ring-O6 lone pair -> C1=O6 oxocarbenium pi bond) is an implicit bond-forming arc required for electron balance (not drawn on the page). The anomeric OCH3 oxygen is drawn protonated (O+ with an added H), i.e. the proton sits on the leaving group. The printed 76% is the relative abundance of the (MH-CH3OH)+ methanol-loss channel for the ribo isomer, which eliminates methanol more readily than the arabo isomer (stereospecific). Charge-site (inductive) 1,1-elimination of methanol from the protonated permethylated pentofuranoside [M+H]+: the ring-oxygen (O6) lone pair forms the C1=O6 oxocarbenium pi bond (anchimeric assistance) while the C1-O7 bond to the protonated anomeric methoxy breaks heterolytically, both of its electrons departing with the neutral methanol. Encoded as two double-barbed (2e) moves; the arrow_check reports the O6 and O7 changes as advisory '(soft)' lone-pair notes, which is expected for heterolytic lone-pair chemistry. Structure encoded as a FLAT/representative furanose skeleton: ribo and arabo are C-2 epimeric diastereomers, but the scan's wedge/hash stereochemistry cannot be assigned to an absolute configuration with confidence, so absolute stereochemistry is not encoded; the electron-pushing is identical for both diastereomers and only the drawn proton disposition and the abundance differ.

No MOD rule in data/mechanisms/rule_index.json maps to Equation 8.31 (only '8.3' is indexed, an unrelated equation). This even-electron [M+H]+ heterolytic 1,1-elimination of methanol is not represented among the current radical-cation MOD fragmentation rules; no cross-link asserted.
